subject: physiology
title: Female reproductive physiology and menstrual cycle

steps.tx: The **ovary** rests a million primordial follicles at birth, recruits and selects under follicle stimulating hormone into a Graafian antral follicle, ovulates at the luteinising hormone surge near day fourteen, sustains progesterone from the corpus luteum, loses most follicles to atresia by apoptosis, counts reserve by anti Mullerian hormone, and makes oestradiol in granulosa cells. Puberty buds breasts at thelarche, bleeds at menarche near twelve and smells at adrenarche, while polycystic ovary syndrome by Rotterdam cysts and anovulation stalls cycles.
steps.say: A girl is born with her lifetime stock of primordial follicles, and each cycle follicle stimulating hormone recruits a cohort from which one Graafian follicle wins, the stages traced in the figure. The luteinising hormone surge ovulates it near day fourteen, the corpus luteum secretes progesterone, and most follicles die quietly by atresia. Anti Mullerian hormone estimates remaining reserve, breast budding starts puberty, and polycystic ovaries stall selection.

vis.alt: Stages of follicle development: primordial, primary, secondary, antral, Graafian follicle, ovulation under the LH surge, corpus luteum making progesterone, and corpus albicans if no pregnancy.
vis.caption: FSH recruits and selects the dominant follicle; the LH surge ovulates; the corpus luteum sustains progesterone for about two weeks.

steps.tx: The menstrual **cycle** rebuilds endometrium proliferatively under oestrogen, ovulates at the luteinising hormone surge with clear mucus, coils secretory glands under progesterone, sheds near eighty millilitres at withdrawal menses, cramps by prostaglandins eased by nonsteroidal drugs, aches mid cycle as mittelschmerz, shifts basal temperature after ovulation, and ferns cervical mucus under oestrogen crystals. Lengths run twenty one to thirty five days with a fixed fourteen day luteal phase, anovulatory cycles bleed as dysfunctional bleeding, and amenorrhoea first excludes pregnancy.
steps.say: Oestrogen rebuilds the lining, its peak triggers the ovulatory surge, and progesterone then ripens secretory glands, the hormone curves plotted in the cycle figure. Withdrawal of progesterone sheds the lining with prostaglandin cramps that anti inflammatory drugs ease, mid pain marks ovulation, and temperature rises afterwards. Cycles span twenty one to thirty five days with a constant two week luteal half, and a missed period first demands a pregnancy test.

vis.alt: Plot of the 28 day menstrual cycle with FSH, LH, oestradiol and progesterone: FSH rises early, oestradiol peaks before ovulation, an LH surge on day 14 triggers ovulation, progesterone peaks in the luteal phase; follicular and luteal phases and the proliferative and secretory endometrium are labelled.
vis.caption: Oestradiol peak triggers the LH surge; LH surge ovulates; progesterone dominates the luteal phase.

steps.tx: In **pregnancy** human chorionic gonadotropin from trophoblast doubles near forty eight hours, progesterone passes from corpus luteum to placenta, oestriol reports the fetoplacental unit, prolactin prepares breasts, oxytocin labours and lets down milk, and morning sickness peaks as gonadotropin peaks. Ectopic pregnancy bleeds adnexally needing culdocentesis history, miscarriage threatens or completes or turns septic, urine tests detect a missed week, ultrasound hears six week hearts, crown rump length dates, and folate four milligrams guards high risk spines.
steps.say: Human chorionic gonadotropin doubles every two days early on, rescues the corpus luteum, then yields progesterone production to the placenta around eight weeks, the handover shown in the pregnancy curves. Oestriol tracks the fetal placental unit, prolactin primes the breast, and oxytocin drives labour and milk ejection. Dating uses crown rump length, hearts appear near six weeks, bleeding demands exclusion of ectopic implantation, and high dose folate protects high risk spines.

vis.alt: Plot of hormone levels across pregnancy: hCG rises from implantation to a peak at about 8 to 10 weeks then falls to a plateau, progesterone shifts from corpus luteum to placenta around weeks 7 to 9 and keeps rising, oestriol rises steadily to term.
vis.caption: hCG peaks at 8 to 10 weeks and then falls; the placenta takes over progesterone from the corpus luteum around weeks 7 to 9.

steps.tx: At **menopause** follicle stimulating hormone runs high as ovaries fail, hot flashes widen from the hypothalamus, vaginal dryness needs moisturisers, bone density falls to treatment thresholds, and hormone replacement trades benefit against clots and strokes, tibolone adding libido at stroke cost and soy phytoestrogens selecting mildly, while failure before forty freezes eggs as premature. Contraception spans pills with venous thrombosis and migraine limits, copper and hormonal intrauterine devices for bleeding, ulipristal or copper emergency cover, and sterilisation needing regret counselling, while postmenopausal bleeding by PALM COEIN alarms to biopsy.
steps.say: When ovaries retire, pituitary drive rises unanswered, flushes disturb sleep, vaginal tissues dry, and bone thins, changes eased selectively by hormone therapy weighed against clot and stroke risks. Failure before forty is premature and may still allow egg freezing. Contraception before menopause ranges from pills limited by migraine and thrombosis to intrauterine devices and emergency ulipristal or copper, and any bleeding after menopause needs endometrial sampling.
